title: Minted, stored, proven — with the dispatch's premise contradicted and one of its expectations unmeetable

snapshot.hauskaMcpServerDirty: unchanged from CP1 — three files modified by an earlier session, none by this lane

minted.tierSource: READ off the pilot row 2a26c318-271d-414c-967d-caba619a6f73 at CP1, not guessed
minted.ownerEmailChoice: A plus-alias on the operator's own inbox. The request suggested exactly this shape and said the choice was the substrate seat's. Chosen because it is textually distinct in the DB — so a rotation or a revoke can never be confused with the pilot row — without inventing an account nobody reads.
minted.mintCall: POST https://hauska-mcp-server-h7gvu7rgcq-uc.a.run.app/admin/keys, header X-Hauska-Admin-Key read from Secret Manager HAUSKA_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_KEY inside the script process

stored.whyThisProjectNotTheRequestsOne: The dispatch overrode the 2026-09-15 request: hauska-prod-497015 holds the store the key is validated against, so the secret moves with hauska-mcp-server at OPS-25 D-7. The request named the dashboards' GCP project, which is being exited.
stored.valueHandling: Returned once by the mint, held in a local, piped to `gcloud secrets create --data-file=-` on STDIN (never argv), never echoed, logged, or written to a file. The script refuses to run at all if the secret already exists, so a re-run cannot silently rotate what lanes read.
stored.assertionsOnTheStoredValue: The script asserts the minted value has the hk_ prefix shape and asserts version 1 exists and is ENABLED. It does NOT read the value back out.

proven.instrument: _inbox/2026-09-18_g135-mint_probe.mjs, this lane's own; the raw value is read from Secret Manager inside the probe and presented in the x-hauska-key header

counts.countingRule: one cell per HTTP request the probe made; each cell is compared against an expected band declared in the instrument before it ran

cells.what: GET /auth/whoami on the MCP with the minted key
GET /api/city-domains?cityKey=bastrop_tx on d12-main-uat WITH the key
cells.body: cityKey=bastrop_tx, displayName 'Bastrop, TX', environment staging, regionCount 11, withRecords 8

cells.what: same key against fixture-city, the OTHER tenant-private pack

proven.theFourDirections: (1) scoped-in tenant readable WITH the key: cell C 200. (2) same route WITHOUT the key: cell D 401. (3) garbage key refused: cell E 401. (4) the SAME key against a DIFFERENT tenant-private pack refused: cell F 403 — this is the direction that proves the credential is tenant-scoped rather than a master key, and it was MEASURED, not declared unmeasurable, because smartcity-dashboards ships two tenant-private packs (bastrop_tx and fixture-city; src/city-pack.test.mjs).
proven.controlsThatMakeThe401sMeaningful: Cell G proves the app is up and the public-free pack still reads with no key, so cells D and E are the gate refusing and not an outage. Cell H separates a gated pack (401) from a nonexistent one (404), so 'bastrop_tx is gated' is distinguishable from 'bastrop_tx does not exist'.

keyIdLinkage.dispatchesExpectation: The dispatch says /auth/whoami must return jurisdiction_tenant=bastrop_tx AND the new key_id.
keyIdLinkage.measured: The deployed route returns only {"anonymous":false,"jurisdiction_tenant":"bastrop_tx"} — there is NO key_id field. Verified by reading the raw body with the key redacted.
keyIdLinkage.howTheLinkageIsEstablishedInstead: A separate instrument, GET /admin/keys, read immediately after the probe: the row key_id=96e40316-0907-49f3-8c6e-d47d9013f02e has last_used_at 2026-09-18T14:47:21.181Z, which is inside this probe's own window. A credential presented by this probe advanced this key_id's last_used_at, which ties the value to the row.
keyIdLinkage.declaredAs: a contradiction of the dispatch's step 4, recorded rather than worked around by claiming a field that does not exist

one_thePremiseIsFalse.dispatchClaims: The only active bastrop_tx key is the operator's pilot key, and no lane-usable credential exists.
one_thePremiseIsFalse.measuredAtCP1: THREE active rows scoped to bastrop_tx: the pilot (2a26c318, created 2026-09-03), 'G-134 lane verification (bastrop_tx)' (acf2cf9f, created 2026-09-15, used once 14s later, apparently never since), and 'G-154 lane verification (machine credential, not a person)' (2510a3ff, created 2026-09-18T14:36:21Z, last_used_at 14:42:18Z — 23 seconds before CP1 read the store, so that lane is using it right now).
one_thePremiseIsFalse.consequence: This lane's mint is deduplication-and-documentation, not first provisioning. The deliverable is unchanged: there was still no DOCUMENTED location (no Secret Manager secret held any bastrop_tx lane credential, and the index read 'REQUESTED, NOT YET MINTED'), which is what the row actually asks for.

three_aSecretNamedUrlHoldsADatabaseDsn.what: While looking for the MCP's HTTP base URL, this lane read the secrets PRODUCTION_HAUSKA_MCP_URL and STAGING_HAUSKA_MCP_URL. Both hold `postgresql://` connection strings with an embedded password, not URLs. Read from the name, not from any code.
three_aSecretNamedUrlHoldsADatabaseDsn.whyItMatters: A secret whose NAME promises one thing and whose VALUE is another invites exactly this: a lane reads it expecting a URL and prints a production database credential.
three_aSecretNamedUrlHoldsADatabaseDsn.disclosure: This lane READ those two values verbatim into this session's terminal before recognising what they were, so the value is now present in this session's harness terminal-output file under C:\Users\cente\.cursor\projects\... . The value appears NOWHERE in any artifact, commit, close or chat message written by this lane, and it was not used for anything.
three_aSecretNamedUrlHoldsADatabaseDsn.notRotated: This lane rotated nothing. Whether that DSN should be treated as exposed and rotated is a planner/operator call, and it is raised as a leave_behind rather than decided here.
three_aSecretNamedUrlHoldsADatabaseDsn.theCorrectInstrument: The MCP HTTP base URL was already recorded at source in this repo — _inbox/2026-09-14_g133-bastrop-verify-access_cp2.json names it and matches the dashboards' HAUSKA_MCP_URL — so the secret never needed to be read.

whatWasNotDone: No product code written, in any repo. hauska-mcp-server is untouched (its three pre-existing dirty files are unchanged).
Nothing deployed. d12-main-uat's active deployment is still 939947a9 at 53ade8a, deployed by the operator's UPDATE_SPEC at 13:39Z, before this lane existed.
The pilot row was not touched, and neither of the other two active bastrop_tx rows was patched or revoked.

The G-135 row's second pass condition — 'a full-shell authenticated probe on bastrop_tx mounts the map iframe' — was NOT run by this lane. It is not in this dispatch's five work steps, and _inbox/2026-09-18_HANDOFF_smartcity_planner.md assigns the three probe commands to the G-154 lane. Declared here because it is a pass condition on this plan row.
